en.headline: Universities launch MentAl Bot to train teachers on student mental health
en.dek: The digital platform, based on WHO standards, starts with 300 teachers and 300 university students across 20 schools.
body: A coalition of researchers from the Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Chinese University of Hong Kong and Hong Kong Shue Yan University, together with the Association of Professional Mental Health and Wellness Education, has launched MentAl Bot, a digital learning platform to help teachers recognise and respond to students' mental health needs.

The project is described as the first systematic mental health training programme in Hong Kong built on the World Health Organization's International Classification of Diseases framework, translating diagnostic concepts into practical material for educators without medical training. Content uses video case studies and gamified interactive modules covering mental health literacy, depression, anxiety and bipolar disorder.

In the first phase starting Thursday, the platform is being rolled out to 300 university students and 300 teachers from 20 secondary, primary and special schools. Organisers said the tool is not intended to turn teachers into clinicians or to diagnose students, but to raise awareness and strengthen the first layer of support in schools. Association chairwoman Amy Lam emphasised that the goal is to reduce stigma and improve early recognition.

zh.headline: 三所大學推出MentAl Bot 助教師辨識學生精神健康需要
zh.dek: 平台以世衛標準為基礎，首階段涵蓋20所學校的300名教師及300名大學生。
body: 理工大學、中文大學、樹仁大學聯同香港心理教育專業協會共同推出精神健康數碼學習平台MentAl Bot，協助教師提升對學生精神健康需要的覺察和辨識能力。
計劃以世界衛生組織國際疾病分類框架為基礎，將專業知識轉化為非醫療背景教師可應用的學習內容，採用生活化情境短片及遊戲化互動，涵蓋精神健康素養、抑鬱症、焦慮症及躁鬱症。主辦單位指，這是本港首個以此分類系統系統化培訓教師的精神健康計劃。
首階段即日起向300名大學生及來自20所中小學和特殊學校的300名教師推出。計劃首席總監何偉倫表示，平台有別於臨床治療工具，會按理解程度提供回饋，並設有前後測以量度成效。協會主席林女士強調，平台並非讓教師成為臨床人員或診斷學生，而是希望減少標籤、加強學校第一層支援。
